claim: Hong-Page simulation (ringworld, n=2000, l=12/20, k=3): 10 random agents beat the 10 best agents (94.53 vs 92.56 at l=12; 50 trials), reproduced by independent authors.
agent_test: Re-run on a toy search task with a pool of prompts: random prompt-set of 10 vs 10 best-on-dev prompts at equal tokens.

claim: The Hong-Page theorem is a possibility statement with a flawed lemma (V must be one-to-one) and does not apply to the experiment; the best-N group is clones of one agent only when the pool is huge.
agent_test: No agent test; use only as caution against citing diversity trumps ability as a law.

claim: Part of the Hong-Page result is randomness plus group size, not diversity: groups built for maximal diversity do worse than random groups; the gap correlates .65 with effective group size; the diversity score can be relabelled hostility.
agent_test: Compare random vs max-different-prompt sets vs best-N prompt sets at equal tokens; report the gap vs effective overlap.

claim: The Hong-Page effect is fragile to landscape structure: on landscapes where ability matters (stairway) high-ability groups win for small groups and simple problems; diversity wins only when problems need more than any one member can do; the original 2001 bit-string model had no diversity advantage.
agent_test: Sort benchmark items by structure (random-like vs structured); test whether best-prompt beats varied prompts on structured items.

claim: Ability-based selection also beats diversity in other models: take-the-best groups beat minimalist (diverse) groups when cue validities differ strongly, even at group size 100; accuracy peaks at intermediate noise.
agent_test: Mix strong and weak solver prompts; check where weak diverse solvers stop adding value.

claim: In LLM mixture-of-agents, sampling the single best model repeatedly (Self-MoA) beat mixing different models: AlpacaEval 2.0 LC 65.7 vs 59.1 (+6.6), average +3.8 over MMLU-redux, CRUX, MATH (verified in paper). Gap search: at matched model quality a low-correlation mix of different models beat Self-MoA by +0.027 on average (range +0.010 to +0.050; MATH-500 +0.020 n.s.; Chen 2026), and in a compute-equalised test Self-MoA with gpt-oss-120b reached 64.1 on GPQA-Diamond, below zero-shot 66.7, but 90.0 on AIME (Fadnavis 2026). So Self-MoA is not uniformly better; the direction depends on quality gap and task.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of N samples from the best model vs N models. Same paper counted three times; needs independent replication.

claim: MoA accuracy is more sensitive to proposer quality than to diversity (Vendi): normalised coefficients MMLU 2.558 vs 1.841, CRUX 4.548 vs 1.421, MATH 4.719 vs 2.839, R2 .685-.771, about 70 mixtures per dataset (verified).
agent_test: Regress accuracy on proposer quality and diversity across prompt-sets of our agent.

claim: The original MoA diversity comparison (multi 61.3 vs single 56.7 at n=6) used Qwen1.5-110B as the single proposer, which is not the best proposer: WizardLM-8x22B alone as proposer scores 63.8, above the 61.3 mix. The two papers are consistent.
agent_test: Always compare a mix to resampling the best single member, not to an arbitrary member.

claim: Cross-family heterogeneity helps debate and ensembles when members are of comparable quality: three different families 91% vs 82% for three copies on GSM8K; ReConcile +6.8 on StrategyQA; Heter-MAD +2.7 to +8.2.
agent_test: Test only if a second model is allowed; with one model the achievable analogue is prompt or approach diversity.

claim: LLM errors are correlated across models and providers: when both wrong, models pick the same wrong answer about 60% (random 1/3); mean error agreement 0.423 (HuggingFace); more accurate models correlate more. Chatbot Arena same-family tie rate 34.9% vs 28.8% cross-family.
agent_test: Measure error overlap of our agent's varied attempts; low overlap is needed for voting to add anything.

claim: LLM outputs are homogeneous: within-model pairwise similarity over 0.8 on 26K open-ended queries, cross-model 0.71-0.82; GPT-3.5 gave zero-variance answers in 6 of 14 Many Labs 2 studies and could not stand in for a population.
agent_test: Measure pairwise embedding similarity among our attempts at default settings vs with diversity operators; the operators must move it.

claim: Prompt-level diversity from one model beats plain self-consistency: DIV-SE 97 vs SC-10 23 on Graph Coloring, 94 vs 73 Blocksworld-3 (GPT-4); DIPPER 7 distinct prompts 57.31% vs 55.76% same-prompt (Qwen2-Math-1.5B). Gap search caveat: in a one-model study at 7-11 equal calls, persona, paraphrase and strategy variants were statistically the same (GPQA 72.7, 72.7, 70.2; McNemar p>0.25), so the gain is not tied to designed approach variation, and prompt variety did not lower error correlation (0.633 vs 0.603).
agent_test: Equal-token: N varied-approach prompts vs N samples of one prompt vs best single approach, with a trace-reading synthesiser and a vote-only arm.

claim: Persona prompts alone do not help: 162 personas gave no MMLU gain over no persona across 4 model families; automatic persona selection was no better than random; Multi-Persona debate was weakest in Smit et al.
agent_test: Do not add persona operators; test approach-diversity instead.

claim: Multi-agent debate adds little beyond majority voting from same-model samples (re-verified from the paper, arXiv 2508.17536): Qwen2.5-7B 7-benchmark average single 0.7205, best MAD 0.7377, voting 0.7691; Llama3.1-8B single 0.6203, best MAD 0.6990, voting 0.7242; centralized MAD below single in both. Debate is modelled as a martingale.
agent_test: Skip debate; compare voting over varied attempts with a one-model debate at equal tokens.

claim: Coverage (any sample correct) scales log-linearly with samples (SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250; MATH Llama-3-8B 82.9% to 98.44%) but majority or reward selection plateaus (40.50% to 41.41%): diversity helps only with a selector (verified).
agent_test: Report pass@k vs selected accuracy for our agent; selector quality is the bottleneck.

claim: Diversity helps only when the selector can pick the best candidate: diverse team + judge 0.810, majority vote 0.496, synthesis 0.179, homogeneous 0.512. Correction: with independent judges the effect attenuates by 53-67% (0.810 to 0.611; 0.929 to 0.726), rank order kept (rho .90). Gap search support: false positives of the verifier cap resampling gains and optimal K is often below 10 (Stroebl 2026); a weighted ensemble of weak verifiers lifted Llama 3.3 70B from 68.4 (first sample) and 72.2 (vote) to 87.7 (Weaver); GPT-4 self-critique fell below plain prompting (Game of 24 5% to 3%) while a sound verifier gave 36-38%.
agent_test: Vary selector quality (tests or independent check vs self-judge) crossed with attempt diversity.

claim: Synthesis or consensus aggregation destroys diversity gains: MoA-style synthesis 0.179; consensus selection in code ensembles falls into a popularity trap while diversity-based selection reaches 95% of an upper bound of up to +83%.
agent_test: Use selection by checks, not blending of attempts.

claim: Epistemic landscape models: a shared non-personalised AI oracle reduces community diversity and lowers outcomes on NK landscapes (N=20, K=5; 1,000 sims). Lazer-Friedman: more social learning gives faster early gains and worse long-run best (second-hand).
agent_test: Limit cross-attempt sharing of partial results early; test sharing delay at equal tokens.

claim: The Weisberg-Muldoon claim that mavericks help followers is contested: Alexander, Himmelreich and Thompson (2015) say it came from modelling errors; a re-implementation reproduced the results but showed high sensitivity to rule details. None of these were opened. Gap search: only the Alexander et al. abstract could be read (full texts blocked); it confirms their conclusion that seeking novelty need not be optimal and that social learning is doubtful in complex landscapes. Still not opened in full.
agent_test: Do not rely on the maverick result; test a forbid-visited-approaches operator directly.

claim: Wisdom of the silicon crowd: median of 12 different LLMs matched 925 human forecasters (Brier .20 vs .19, p=.850, verified); LLMs show acquiescence bias; models improve (GPT-4 .17 to .14, p=.003) when shown the human median.
agent_test: Aggregation of independent forecasts; not directly testable with one model.

claim: Human team meta-analyses give small effects: task-related diversity r=.10 (Horwitz and Horwitz 2007, 35 studies), task-oriented r=.04 (Joshi and Roh 2009), job-related r=.05 (Bell 2011); bio-demographic about zero. The 2024 registered-report meta-analysis (615 reports, 2,638 effects) finds all average |r|<.1, larger for R&D teams (.058 vs .020) and creativity/innovation outcomes (.056 vs .020).
agent_test: Use as a prior: expect low single-digit gains from diversity alone; larger only on creative or complex tasks.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Reasoning models simulate several internal perspectives; steering one conversational feature doubled Countdown accuracy 27.1% to 54.8% (verified), -10 gave 23.8%.
agent_test: Closest evidence that one model gains from internal diversity; try the prompt-level analogue on our scaffold.

claim: Degeneration of thought: after confidence, self-reflection stops generating new ideas; MAD with a judge raised GPT-3.5 counter-intuitive arithmetic from 26.0 to 37.0.
agent_test: Check whether reflection on its own output changes the answer rate at equal tokens.

claim: Large same-model ensembles scale with count: Llama2-13B at ensemble 15 matches Llama2-70B on GSM8K; gains grow with task difficulty.
agent_test: Plot accuracy vs number of samples at equal tokens against one longer attempt.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Within one model, varied prompts do not lower error overlap: mean pairwise error correlation 0.633 (perturbed) vs 0.603 (identical prompt) on GPQA-Diamond and 0.571 vs 0.607 on LCB-Hard; Self-MoA samples of the best model show intra-model error correlation 0.80 vs 0.42 across different models at matched quality.
agent_test: Measure pairwise error correlation of N attempts from our model with and without operators on a dev set.

claim: A hard ceiling for any attempt pool: a vote, router or cascade cannot beat 1 minus delta, the share of items where every attempt fails (MATH-500 delta=0.052; GPQA free-response 0.127). Pairwise error correlation cannot identify delta.
agent_test: Compute delta over attempts on the dev set; if delta is large, add information, not attempts.

claim: Gain from varied attempts at equal calls comes mostly from the aggregator reading minority traces, not from the variation: minority-only traces 73.2% vs full traces 72.2%; answer-only inputs fall to the vote baseline; synthesis beat SC by +2.5 (GPQA), +6.1 (BBH-3), +5.3 (LCB-Hard greedy).
agent_test: Compare vote-only vs trace-reading synthesis over the same varied attempts at equal tokens.

claim: Dense early sharing between LLM agents shrinks diversity and buries unique facts: Vendi/N falls 1.03 to 0.47 as agents go 3 to 7; hidden-profile accuracy 30.1% vs 80.7% for single agents with full information; blind independent writing (NGT) gives the highest initial diversity. Human data agree in direction (clustering raised convergence on wrong answers).
agent_test: Run attempts independently, share raw evidence only after, withhold conclusions; test at equal tokens.

claim: Lazer-Friedman result (efficient networks win short-run, lose long-run on complex landscapes) was not opened in full; Shore et al. report Mason and Watts found the opposite structural cause (clustering reduces exploration).
agent_test: No agent test until the original is read.

claim: Task format changes diversity headroom: the same GPQA-Diamond questions give delta=0.127 free-response while multiple choice hides shared failures; team meta-analysis effect is larger for complex and creative tasks. No paper shows an online detector of stairway vs random landscapes in LLM tasks.
agent_test: Compare diversity gains on checkable free-response vs multiple-choice versions of the same items.

claim: Heterogeneity beats homogeneous scaling at small N in one study (2 diverse agents match or exceed 16 homogeneous; MIX beats best single model by up to +14.28 points at N=8 on 126 Formal Logic questions), but strong closed models showed negative scaling (gpt-4.1-mini debate 50.79 to 42.86).
agent_test: Treat as direction only; prompt-only heterogeneity is confounded with models and tools.
